body.statement: On every observable law satisfying Conditions 2--3 of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki (2026) that is compatible with the selected four-response-type model, the rigid value returned by \(\mathscr A\) equals the PN/PS value obtained from their Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33). The same atlas is defined on singular and boundary inputs not covered by those regular conditions, including design-A support-face strata with rank loss, coincident endpoints, inactive rows, or forced-zero incident coefficients and analogous design-B strata governed by response-level shared-\(Z\) residual forests. It reports incompatibility when the full fiber is empty; on every nonempty such fiber it returns either a target-rigidity certificate with an exact value or a legal target-changing full-SCM certificate.
body.justification: The theorem verifies published regular formulas on compatible laws and proves that the same structural compiler handles all singular and boundary inputs.
body.gap: The anchor paper does not supply a full-fiber classifier when its regular inversions fail.
body.consumer: Users retain the published value on its regular compatible domain and receive an exact rigidity, countermodel, or incompatibility certificate elsewhere.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)\) denote the pair in Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33) of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki. Consider a compatible observable law satisfying their Conditions 2--3. Every member of the present full fiber satisfies their Condition 1 by the defining response, selection, and proxy factorization. The cited regular-identification lemma therefore gives
\[
\tau(\vartheta)=R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)
\qquad\text{for every compatible }\vartheta. \tag{15}
\]
Compatibility makes the fiber nonempty, and the cited lemma includes the positive observed probabilities needed for every conditioning and division in (15). Hence the full target image is \(\{R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)\}\). The full-rigidity theorem makes \(\mathscr A\) declare the fiber rigid and return precisely this published value.

For any singular or boundary input, the completed structural enumeration first tests compatibility. If no chart is nonempty, its equality with the cycle fiber proves that the full fiber is empty by the cycle-to-SCM lift, and the compiler reports incompatibility. Otherwise, the rank-one normal forms, oriented rank-two faces, endpoint-incidence refinements, and support signs assign every design-A cycle point to a chart. In design B, the zero or active residual refinements additionally assign every compatible point to a residual forest and impose its component scales, cycle product, and relevance. The full-rigidity theorem then gives exactly one of two alternatives on the nonempty fiber: all one-copy component projections agree at an exact target value, or two sampled points lift to legal target-changing SCMs. This proves regular-domain agreement and the compatible boundary-coverage claim without applying the regular inversion outside its support.
